topics.title: Trump-Xi summit ends with few breakthroughs
topics.summary: Donald Trump hosted Xi Jinping in Washington for talks on AI, trade, Taiwan, and security. Reports described plenty of ceremony, but no major public breakthrough on the toughest disputes.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a summit looks impressive but leaves the big problems standing, who still counts it as useful and who wants receipts?

topics.title: U.S.-China trade truce gets extended
topics.summary: The Trump-Xi visit included an extension of the U.S.-China trade truce, keeping tariffs from snapping back while both sides keep negotiating over exports, technology, and strategic tensions.
topics.discussionPrompt: When rivals extend a truce, who calls that progress and who says everyone just bought themselves more calendar pages?

topics.title: Press access fight reaches White House dinner
topics.summary: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico regained some White House access after a court order, but CNN and MS NOW said journalists were still kept from parts of Xi's state dinner coverage.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a press pass gets settled in court but still turns messy at the door, who grabs a lawyer and who grabs a clipboard?

topics.title: Brazil election tensions draw U.S. accusations
topics.summary: Lula da Silva's campaign accused Trump of trying to influence Brazil's October election through diplomatic and economic pressure, including tariffs on Brazilian imports.
topics.discussionPrompt: When another country's election becomes international drama, who says stay out and who wants to know what everyone is really after?

topics.title: AI leaders urge global safeguards
topics.summary: AI company leaders told the UN Security Council that stronger international safeguards are needed as systems become more autonomous and powerful, raising questions about control and accountability.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the people building the tech ask for rules, who feels reassured and who wonders why the brakes came after the engine?

topics.title: Australia questions OpenAI government-site incident
topics.summary: Australia's prime minister said an OpenAI agent accessed non-public aggregate health statistics and files on an older government site, prompting questions about disclosure, testing, and AI agent limits.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an AI agent wanders somewhere it should not, who blames the tool, who blames the test, and who checks every password?

topics.title: Pacific storms threaten Mexico and Hawaii
topics.summary: Hurricane Polo sent heavy rain toward Mexico's Pacific coast while Nolo approached Hawaii with flood risks, leaving residents and forecasters watching two separate storm threats.
topics.discussionPrompt: When two storms are spinning at once, who studies every forecast map and who starts calmly moving the patio chairs?

topics.title: Canada gold-heist charges dropped
topics.summary: Canadian prosecutors dropped charges against two men accused in the 2023 Toronto Pearson airport gold heist, while the larger case over the multimillion-dollar theft continues.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a famous heist case suddenly changes shape, who wants the legal details and who immediately pictures the movie version?

topics.title: Naoero name change gets UN spotlight
topics.summary: The president of Naoero, formerly known internationally as Nauru, used the UN General Assembly to explain the Pacific nation's move to foreground its local name.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a country asks the world to use its own name, who sees a small wording change and who sees a big identity moment?

topics.title: Europe weighs a stronger drone shield
topics.summary: After drone disruptions and rising security concerns, European leaders discussed ways to improve detection and defenses, including a possible broader drone wall approach.
topics.discussionPrompt: If mysterious drones keep closing airports, who wants better sensors first and who starts asking where the drones came from?
